Team Synergy: Building a Comp That Works

Five strong champions don't always make a strong team. Learn to balance damage types, frontline, engage, peel and wave clear, and how the main team composition types win.

Why your five picks matter together

A team of five carries with no tank gets run over. A team of five tanks can't kill anyone. Good teams cover the basics and share a plan. You don't need a perfect comp in solo queue, but filling one obvious gap in your team often matters more than picking the 'best' champion on the tier list.

The good news: you only need to check a few things. That's what this guide is about.

Balance your damage

If your team deals only physical damage, the enemy builds armor and your damage melts away. The same is true for all-magic teams and magic resist. Aim for at least one or two strong sources of each damage type.

Mid lane is usually where this gets fixed. If your top, jungle and ADC are all AD, an AP mid like Lux, Syndra or Ahri keeps the enemy from stacking armor. If your team already has lots of magic damage, an AD mid like Yasuo balances it out.

Pro tipHovering helps here too. If you see three AD champions locked on your team, tell them you'll go AP mid before the last picks happen.

Frontline, engage and peel

Most winning teams have someone in each of these jobs. One champion can do two of them.

JobWhat it meansExamplesWithout it
FrontlineStands in front and absorbs damageOrnn, Sejuani, Malphite, BraumYour carries get hit first and die
EngageStarts fights on your termsLeona, Malphite, Jarvan IV, OriannaYou can't force a fight when you're ahead
PeelProtects your carries from diversJanna, Lulu, BraumAssassins and divers kill your damage dealers
Wave clearKills minion waves quickly, from rangeZiggs, Malzahar, JinxYou can't defend towers or siege safely

Early game vs late game

Some champions are strongest early (Draven, Lee Sin, Renekton), others scale into late-game monsters (Kayle, Kassadin, Smolder). Neither is wrong, but your team needs to know which plan it's on.

  • Early-game team: fight for every early objective, dive, take towers, and end before 30 minutes.
  • Scaling team: farm safely, trade objectives instead of contesting bad fights, and win late.
  • Mixed: the early champions create space while the scalers farm.
Common mistakeA team of five late-game champions can fall too far behind to ever reach the late game. If your team is all scaling, a safe early-game pick (or at least a good laner) helps you survive.

The main comp types

CompHow it winsExample pieces
Engage / teamfightBig area crowd control into big area damageMalphite + Orianna + Miss Fortune
PokeChips enemies down from range before fights or siegesZiggs + Jayce + Ezreal + Karma
PickCatches one enemy out of position, then takes objectives 5v4Ahri + Blitzcrank + Ashe
Protect the carryKeeps one hyper-carry alive while it destroys everythingJinx + Lulu + Braum
Split pushA strong duelist pressures a side lane while the team holdsFiora + Ziggs + Janna

Once you know your comp type, the Win Conditions & Team Comps guide explains how to play it.

Checking what your team lacks

When you're picking in the second half of the draft, run this quick checklist:

  1. Who is our frontline?
  2. Who starts fights?
  3. Do we have both magic and physical damage?
  4. Who clears waves and defends towers?
  5. Are we an early or a late team?

Then pick the champion from your own pool that fills the biggest gap. If your team has no AP, play your AP champion. If you're a support and there's no frontline, pick an engage tank over an enchanter.

Example: fixing a draft

Your team picked Jayce top, Kindred jungle and Ezreal bot, and you're picking mid, with your support last. Run the checklist:

  • Frontline: none so far. Your support should probably be a tank.
  • Engage: none. Again, the support can fix this.
  • Damage: all physical. This is the gap you can fill.
  • Wave clear and range: Jayce and Ezreal already poke from long range.

The team is leaning toward poke, so a long-range AP mid like Ziggs or Lux adds magic damage and fits the plan. Then tell your support: "We have no frontline, can you play a tank or an engage support?" With Leona or Braum added, you have a poke comp with someone to stand in front, a much better draft than five squishy champions.

Pro tipYou don't need to be the last pick to fix a draft. Say what the team is missing in chat early, and the players after you can fill it.

Key takeaways

  • Have at least one or two strong sources of both magic and physical damage.
  • Check your team for frontline, engage, peel and wave clear.
  • Know whether your team wins early or late, and play to that plan.
  • Learn the comp types (engage, poke, pick, protect, split push) and how each one wins.
  • When picking late, fill your team's biggest gap with a champion you know.
